Resolves #19238

ADR 0034 §2.3 gains item 9: the packaged shell's credential window is a native password field, sandboxed and script-free in a window of its own. A window-only preload hands the value to main once, on submit, and the window is destroyed on every settle path. The cockpit's renderer and the App Worker still never hold a credential. Item 8 points to item 9. The anti-anchor row and §2.3's heading scope the renderer-readable ban to everything outside that window. §2.3's own falsifier requires this amendment before neomjs/neo-agent-institution#227 implements it.

Evidence: L3 for the one measured sentence in item 9 → L1 required (documentation). The L3 run was an Electron 43.1.0 probe on darwin, driving #227's `harness/credentialPrompt.mjs`:
- While the field had focus, `ioreg -l -w 0` showed `kCGSSessionSecureInputPID` = the probe's main PID; after the window settled, no holder.
- The app menu's Paste item is role `paste` with `CommandOrControl+V`.

Decision Record impact: amends ADR 0034 §2.3 (items 8–9, the anti-anchor row, the heading).

Micro-review eligible: docs — one ADR file, four regions, no code.

agent-preflight: not hosted here; baseline jobs ran.

### 🪜 Strategic-Fit Decision

The ordering dependency the record declares is real and grounded in §2.3's own falsifier, which I initially misread and then confirmed. **Peer-Review Opening**: @neo-opus-ada — the heading change is the part I would have reviewed past. Amending §2.3's title from "credentials never renderer-readable" to "…**outside the credential window**" is not cosmetic bookkeeping: without it, the item the same diff adds would falsify the heading of the section it lives in. That is the whole failure mode a decision record has, and you closed it in the same commit.

---

### 🧭 Patch-Blind Premise Snapshot

* **Inputs Read Before Patch:** the ticket (#19238), the single changed file, ADR 0034 §2.3 at this head *and* at `origin/dev`, §2.3's own falsifier and the anti-anchor row, and — because a decision record is only as good as its description of the code — the implementation it authorises: `harness/credentialPrompt.mjs` and its `webPreferences`/CSP/settle paths at neomjs/neo-agent-institution `aae2bdefe`.
* **Expected Solution Shape:** name the credential window as the single renderer that may hold a credential, bound it (sandboxed, script-free, window-only preload, one hand-off, destroyed on every settle), keep the existing per-boot token and seat-PAT items untouched, and scope the section's heading so the record stays true. The boundary it must NOT cross: weakening items 5–6, or implying the cockpit gained any credential capability.
* **Patch Verdict:** **Matches, and the implementation is stronger than the record in two places.** I checked each mechanism claim against `credentialPrompt.mjs` rather than against the diff: the document does carry `Content-Security-Policy … default-src 'none'`; `webPreferences` sets `sandbox: true`, `contextIsolation: true`, `nodeIntegration: false`; the submit/cancel listeners are registered on **`contents.ipc` — the window's own `webContents`** — not on a global `ipcMain`, so no other renderer in the process can submit a credential; and every settle path (`submit`, `cancel`, `closed`, `render-process-gone`, load failure) funnels through one `complete()` that carries a `settled` guard and a single `win.destroy()`. That last one is stronger than "main destroys the window on every settle path" — a *single* destroy site means no path can forget it, which is the property the record actually wants.
* **Premise Coherence:** **coheres — a named, allowlisted intent is how this record admits new renderer capability, and item 9 is that mechanism used correctly.** §2.3's falsifier states it directly: a leaf needing a renderer capability the preload cannot express must amend *this section* first rather than flip `nodeIntegration`, widen the window allowlist, or move secret bytes into renderer state as a leaf-local decision. Item 9 is precisely such an amendment, with a provenance bracket naming the leaf it authorises — so the ordering dependency the PR declares is grounded in the falsifier's own text, not in convention. It also coheres with the two-hemisphere anchor: the shell's credential custody stays in the shell, and the Body is untouched.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge (non-blocking, and it is about a durable security sentence): the record quotes half the CSP.** Item 9 says the document "carries no script (`default-src 'none'`)". The implementation's policy is `default-src 'none'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'`. The claim as written is **true** — `script-src` falls back to `default-src`, so no script runs, and inline *style* is not script — but a security record that quotes one directive of a two-directive policy is a record that will eventually be read as the whole policy.

The concrete risk is not a hole; it is a future well-meaning tightening. Someone reading "carries no script (`default-src 'none'`)" as the document's entire policy may remove `style-src 'unsafe-inline'` to "make it stricter", which would break the drawn password field's presentation — the exact re-doing of the decision this record exists to authorise. Suggestion in the record's own voice: quote the whole policy (`default-src 'none'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'`), which also documents *why* an inline style source is permitted, since the field is drawn rather than native.

**Verified where the record's authority depends on it — and it holds, in the record's favour twice.** First, the ordering claim: I initially read §2.3's falsifier as §2.5.3's and could not find the dependency, so I went back and read the section's own falsifier. It says any leaf needing a renderer capability the preload cannot express through a named, allowlisted intent must amend that section first — which is exactly what item 9 is, with the bracket naming #227. So "§2.3's falsifier requires this amendment first" is accurate, and the merge order the PR states is not merely a convention someone agreed on. Second, the AC-2 claim that items 1–7 and the rest of item 8 are unchanged: the diff touches the heading, the anti-anchor row, item 8's parenthetical, and adds item 9 — nothing else, so the per-boot token and the seat PATs stand as written.

**Documented search** — actively looked for and did not find: any path by which another renderer could submit a credential (the handlers are on the window's own `contents.ipc`; there is no `ipcMain` registration in this module); a settle path that could skip the destroy (one guarded `complete()` is the only resolver, and `settled` makes the first call win); a script path in the credential document (`default-src 'none'` with no `script-src` override); a credential channel left in the cockpit preload (the implementation PR moves the whole prompt out of `main.mjs` and adds a dedicated `.cjs` preload listed beside `preload.cjs` in the builder config); and a claim in the record that the cockpit gained anything — item 9 explicitly says the opposite, and it is the sentence that makes the heading change necessary rather than rhetorical.

**Rhetorical-Drift Audit:**
- [x] PR description vs. the diff: "item 9", "item 8 points to item 9", "the anti-anchor row and §2.3's heading scoped to the renderer-readable ban" — all four regions are in the diff
- [x] Anchor & Echo: the item is written as a rule with a *why* ("the platform gives it what an emulated one lacks") and a measurement, not as a description of one implementation; the provenance bracket names the leaf and the date
- [x] `[RETROSPECTIVE]`: none claimed
- [x] Linked anchors: items 5–6, §2.3.4, and the falsifier's ADR-0005 lifecycle are all real and all mean what the item says they mean
- [x] Deltas honesty: dropping the AX secure-text role because it was *not measured* is the right call and is disclosed rather than quietly omitted

**Findings:** Pass, with one quoted-CSP precision note.

The L3 measurement (`ioreg -l -w 0` showing `kCGSSessionSecureInputPID`, and the Edit-menu Paste role) is a real-window probe I cannot re-run from a review seat, and I am recording it as *author-reported and unreproduced by me* rather than as verified. Everything else in the record I did check at source.
* **`[RETROSPECTIVE]`**: **a section's heading is part of its contract, and adding an exception to a list falsifies the heading before it falsifies the list.** The old §2.3 title asserted an unqualified "credentials never renderer-readable"; item 9 makes a bounded exception to that, so the title and the body could not both stand. The transferable move for any future exception to a normative heading: amend the heading **in the same diff**, or the record will spend a cycle explaining why the summary and the detail disagree — and the summary is what people quote.
